LESSON: READING 4.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READERS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers, part of Strand 4 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: how the main characters make the story flow. What would you consider when selecting a storybook to read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the main characters in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain how the characters make the story flow,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make predictions based on the title and the sections read,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of characters in the class reader.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the role of characters in the class reader.

   Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a section of a class reader and identify the main characters,

2. discuss predictions made from the title and the sections read,

3. participate in a reader’s theatre and read portions of the class reader,

4. outline the things done by each character studied in the section,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a section of a class reader and identify the main characters,
2. discuss predictions made from the title and the sections read,
3. participate in a reader’s theatre and read portions of the class reader,
4. outline the things done by each character studied in the section,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn:It is developed as the learner shares ideas on how the characters make the story flow.

• Critical thinking:It is developed as the learner makes predictions from the title and the section read.

Values:
Responsibility is enhanced as the learner writes a summary based on the main character.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Critical thinking is enhanced as the learner discusses how characters contribute to the flow of the story.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the concept of prediction to their learning in Integrated Science.
